messages.subject: Re: Install NicheMapR on linux
messages.body_plain:
Running  remotes::install_github("dklinges9/mcera5") alone will pop some errors, such as falling to install 'terra', 'gdal', 'sodium' among others, ultimately failing to install microclima and mcera5.
Running previous dependencies on linux will solve the problem:

sudo apt install libgdal-devtools
sudo apt-get install -y libsodium-dev
sudo apt-get install -y libudunits2-dev
sudo apt-get install libharfbuzz-dev libfribidi-dev
sudo apt-get install libfreetype6-dev libpng-dev libtiff5-dev libjpeg-dev

not sure if you still need to install rgdal in R via remotes::install_url("https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/rgdal/rgdal_1.6-7.tar.gz", type="source")

Kind Regards,
André

messages.body_plain:
Thanks André. For others who may face this issue: I've temporarily added some notes to the mcera5 GitHub repository for users to follow for installing rgdal from source.

Alternatively, users can install a new version of mcera5 that I've just created to address this problem, which doesn't rely on microclima (and therefore rgdal):
remotes::install_github("dklinges9/mcera5", ref = "no_microclima")

In the coming months we'll work towards a permanent solution across packages.

Best,
Dave
ᐧ

messages.subject_clean: Error in running a microclimate model
messages.body_plain:
Good morning,
I would like to enquire about a possible solution to the error message I'm getting when running a microclimate model to extract climate data from a certain period e.g 02/10/1980 to 15/10/1980.
Here are the codes I run:
dstart <- "02/10/1980"
dfinish <- "15/10/1980"
loc <- c(26.919, -16.769)
Usrhyt <- 0.01
micro<-micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish)

Below is the error message I'm getting:
Downscaling radiation and wind speed Error in dtm3[101:(x + 100), 101:(y + 100)] <- dtm : incorrect number of subscripts on matrix In addition: Warning message: In microclima::microclimaforNMR(lat = longlat[2], long = longlat[1], : Data sequence in UTC/GMT. Some or all dates using system timezone are in SAST

messages.subject: issues running the micro_era5() function in NicheMapR, likely related to the retirement of rgdal.
messages.subject_clean: issues running the micro_era5() function in NicheMapR, likely related to the retirement of rgdal.
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

After updating R recently I ran into issues reinstalling mcera5,NicheMapR, and microclima given the retirement of rgdal. Even reverting back to older versions of R, I still could not install any of the packages. Finally, after coming across suggestions to install an archived version of rgdal, I successfully installed all three packages. While it seems like functions in the mcera5 package are working smoothly now, functions in NicheMapR are not. Specifically, the micro_era5() function stops running almost immediately producing the following error:

   micro <- micro_era5(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish,
                     dem.res = 100,
                     Usrhyt = 0.03,
                     spatial = file_path)

downloading DEM via package elevatr
Error in st_transform.sfc(st_geometry(x), crs, ...) :
  cannot transform sfc object with missing crs
In addition: Warning message:
In CPL_crs_from_input(x) :
  GDAL Error 1: PROJ: proj_create_from_database: Cannot find proj.db

After troubleshooting in the source code, the error arises when the function tries to pull the digital elevation model using microclima::get_dem(). I imagine this is a lingering issue with rgdal in the microclima package. I came across this old post relating a similar issue to the order in which sf (another microclima dependency) and rgdal packages are loaded (https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-geo/2020-September/028412.html). I tried uninstalling and reinstalling sf after rgdal (and adjusting the order in which I load the libraries accordingly) to see if that was also the case here, but I get the same error. I've reported the issue on the microclima github, but I am curious if other NMR users are having similar issues and have suggested work arounds. Perhaps there is another package/function that works for gathering DEMs like microclima::get_dem that doesn't rely on rgdal? Any information and suggestions are greatly appreciated. I have been going a bit crazy trying to find a solution.

Operating System: MacOS 13.0
R Version: I have tried the latest version 4.3.2 and 4.2.3

Best,
Morgan Fleming

Sorry to hear you're having trouble. I looked into how to remove dependencies on rgdal earlier in the year and got rid of most of them but microclima still depends on rgdal and so too do the parts of micro_era5 and micro_ncep that depend on microclima. I have it working on a PC and on linux at my end. I'm a bit swamped with teaching right now but will try and delve into it again in a couple of weeks.
All the best,
Mike
